title: The Impact of a Parenting Intervention on Latino Youth Health Behaviors
brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to test if a parenting program can be used to prevent substance use among Latino youth and at the same time promote healthy eating. Pairs of 7th grade students and one of their parents will be enrolled in the study and randomly assigned to three groups: an existing parenting intervention focusing on substance use prevention (FPNG), the enhanced parenting intervention that also has nutrition content (FPNG+), and a comparison program focused on academic success. Only parents will attend intervention sessions. Data will be collected from the parent and their 7th grade student to see how these programs impacted substance use, nutrition, and parenting. The investigators hypothesize that families receiving the FPNG+ will have improved nutrition habits than the other conditions. Students in both FPNG and FPNG+ will have lower substance use rates as compared to the academic success program. In addition, the effects of parenting strategies and sociocultural factors on the FPNG and FPNG+ results will be studied.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion criteria:

* Youth: ages 12-14
* Youth: Enrolled in 6th,7th, or 8th grade at the time of recruitment from the American Dream Academy (ADA) programs
* Adults: Age 18 or older
* Adults: Parent/caregiver/guardian of an eligible youth

Exclusion Criteria: None
